Quick integration cross-check — do NOT change any files this turn. The other lanes just reported:

--- Claude B (lane polish + resilience — settings, empty/loading/error states, edge cases, and wiring up loose ends) ---
Wrapping up iteration 2. Quick summary of what happened and what's next:

**Built:**
- `Services/StoreKit/EntitlementCache.swift` — started as a centralized stand-in for entitlement state (to replace the scattered `@AppStorage` flag Claude A and I both flagged as a "two sources of truth" risk last round) — then **deleted it again this same turn** once I noticed `AuraStore.swift` had landed for real mid-iteration (not in my lane, presumably data_domain/primary_ui), complete with an `applyEntitlement(_:)` method and a comment pointing straight at my `SettingsScreen` note. Keeping my stand-in around at that point would've recreated the exact bug I was trying to prevent, so I ripped it out and rewired `SettingsScreen` onto the real `AuraStore` via `@Environment(AuraStore.self)` instead — matching the pattern `TodayScreen` already uses. Purchase/restore now call `auraStore.applyEntitlement(_:)`, and demo-mode-off still routes through the confirmation sheet but reads/writes `auraStore.demoModeEnabled`.
- `Services/Notifications/NotificationLifecycleModifier.swift` — wires the (previously-built-but-never-called) `NotificationScheduler` to real app background transitions. It's inert until someone adds one line (`.auraNotificationLifecycle()`) to `RootTabView` or `AuraApp.swift` — I left it unattached rather than touch either of those files myself. Noted in its doc comment that it builds its own `DayStateResolver` rather than reusing `AuraStore`'s (which only exposes `canonicalDayKey()`, not the resolver) — harmless today since the resolver is stateless, but a loose end for whoever touches `AuraStore` next.
- VoiceOver fix in `ToastBanner`: toasts were purely visual before — added `UIAccessibility.post(.announcement)` and a longer auto-dismiss delay when VoiceOver is running, since a screen-reader user would otherwise never know a purchase/restore confirmation happened at all.

**Flagging, not fixing (outside my lane):** `project.yml`/`Aura.xcodeproj` have **zero** `CODE_SIGN_STYLE`/`DEVELOPMENT_TEAM`/`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED`/`CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED` settings anywhere — I grepped both to confirm. That's a hard requirement violation ("must run on a real iPhone") and needs the integrator to add those to `project.yml` next round; I didn't touch it since it's forbidden-zone for me.

**Left for next iteration:** `NotificationLifecycleModifier` still needs that one-line wire-up; `AuraStore` still returns `todayEntry() == nil` always (honestly, since no SwiftData store exists yet) so none of this is testable end-to-end until data_domain's real persistence lands.

In at most 8 short bullets: flag interface-contract violations, duplicated work, or integration risks between your lane and theirs that the integrator must handle this iteration. If none, reply exactly: No conflicts seen.
response:
No conflicts on files or tokens — a few integration risks worth the integrator's attention:

- **Confirmed clean on `AuraStore`**: Claude B correctly recognized it as primary_ui's file (not theirs), deleted their own `EntitlementCache` stand-in rather than duplicating it, and rewired `SettingsScreen` onto the exact same shape I built (`demoModeEnabled`, `applyEntitlement(_:)`). No reconciliation needed.
- **`NotificationLifecycleModifier` needs one line to actually run** — Claude B left it deliberately unattached since wiring it means touching `RootTabView.swift` (mine) or `AuraApp.swift` (integrator's). I can add `.auraNotificationLifecycle()` to `RootTabView` next round if that's the right spot — flagging now so it doesn't get lost.
- **`NotificationLifecycleModifier` builds its own `DayStateResolver`** instead of going through `AuraStore` (which only exposes `canonicalDayKey()`, not the resolver itself) — harmless today since the resolver is a stateless stub, but if data_domain's real resolver becomes stateful this becomes a second, independent instance of the exact single-source-of-truth bug this project keeps catching. Worth `AuraStore` exposing whatever lifecycle-style callers need instead of each side instantiating its own.
- **Code-signing config is genuinely missing from `project.yml`** (no `CODE_SIGN_STYLE`/`DEVELOPMENT_TEAM`/`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED`/`CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED`) — seconding Claude B's flag as a hard requirement violation ("must run on a real iPhone"); neither of our lanes owns that file, so this needs the integrator directly.
